Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: one transparent PNG sprite for a 2D garden game.
Input image 1 is the style and identity reference. Use ONLY its upper-left tree-stump house as the reference object; omit the other three atlas objects.
Primary request: redraw that same warm, hand-painted tree-stump house as a naturally tall, complete tree house, not a stretched bitmap. Its eventual in-game display is approximately 606 pixels wide by 710 pixels high. Preserve the recognizable golden cut trunk top, warm orange-brown sculpted bark, dark brown outline, moss touches, a few small green leafy branches near the upper part, and spreading roots at the bottom. Preserve the reference's colors, painterly brushwork, lighting, and slightly three-quarter frontal view.
Composition: one whole isolated object, portrait proportions close to width:height 606:710, centered with a small transparent margin on all sides. All roots and leafy tips fully visible. Roots meet a common ground baseline, but do not paint ground or a cast shadow outside the object. Natural coherent anatomy and bark detail from crown to roots, with no vertically smeared or elongated texture.
Critical gameplay opening: a huge unobstructed open dark-brown tree hollow. Measure these percentages relative to the entire visible tree-house object bounds. The hollow begins at about 24% of the object's height and continues to about 88%. Its horizontal center is approximately 54% of the object's width. At 43% of the object's height, the clear dark inner opening MUST extend at least from 45% to 67% of the object's width, leaving a wide empty flight passage. Make the upper arch broad enough to satisfy this. Bees will enter from the left in the game, so keep the opening visually easy to approach and clearly open. Draw a natural bottom threshold near 88% of object height and solid roots below it, rather than stretching the hollow floor into a long vertical tunnel.
Background: actual transparent alpha, including outside and between branches; the dark interior is opaque painted dark brown, not a transparency hole.
Avoid: bees, birds, other characters, doors, windows, bells, text, numbers, signage, props, a scene/background, extra objects, a sprite sheet, a ground plane, white or colored background, detached pieces, blur, or watermark.
Output: a single production-ready tree-house sprite on a genuinely transparent PNG background.
